title: regional-burst-buffer-and-unit-econ-notes
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a different angle on capacity planning: sizing an always-on baseline + burst buffer per region while explicitly modeling the cost per 1M tokens under different GPU procurement mixes (on-demand, reserved, spot). The emphasis here is on the "friction" costs that reduce effective throughput (cold starts, preemption compute lost, KV-cache warming) and how those shift unit economics at different burst profiles.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Base approach: keep a small steady-state slab to meet sustained QPS and a burst buffer that absorbs P95-P99 demand spikes.
- Spot is attractive for long tail bursts but preemption friction (lost work + restart time) increases $/1M tokens for short, high-churn bursts.
- Use regional arithmetic (tokens/sec per GPU) + effective uptime factor to convert $/GPU-hour into $/1M tokens.
- Recommended starting config: regional baseline = 1.15 * sustained-GPU-need; burst pool = extra capacity sized to P99 spike for 30s–3min windows, backed 70% spot / 30% reserved in NA/EU; tilt more reserved in APAC.

Assumptions (these are placeholders — replace with bench numbers for the target model family):
- GPU type modeled: NVIDIA A100 80GB equivalence. Replace with H100 if applicable.
- Effective sustained throughput per GPU (tokens/sec): small-model (7B) = 420 t/s; medium-model (30B) = 150 t/s; large-model (70B) = 58 t/s.
- Effective utilization factor (friction): baseline steady requests: 0.92 (8% overhead), burst/preempt-prone: 0.78 (22% overhead).
- Regional raw GPU $/hour (example):
  - NA: on-demand $3.20, reserved (1yr) $2.05, spot $1.10
  - EU: on-demand $3.75, reserved $2.40, spot $1.30
  - APAC: on-demand $4.15, reserved $2.65, spot $1.55

How we convert to $ / 1M tokens (working formula):
1) tokens_per_gpu_hour = tokens/sec * 3600 * utilization_factor
2) $/1M tokens = (gpu_hour_price / tokens_per_gpu_hour) * 1,000,000

Example calculations (rounded):
Model: medium (30B), throughput = 150 t/s
- tokens_per_gpu_hour (steady util 0.92) = 150 * 3600 * 0.92 = 497,040 tokens/hr (~0.497M)
- tokens_per_gpu_hour (burst util 0.78) = 150 * 3600 * 0.78 = 421,200 tokens/hr (~0.421M)

NA region:
- On-demand: $3.20/hr => $/1M tokens (steady) = 3.20 / 0.497 = $6.44 per 1M tokens
- Reserved: $2.05/hr => reserved steady = 2.05 / 0.497 = $4.12 per 1M tokens
- Spot: $1.10/hr => spot burst = 1.10 / 0.421 = $2.61 per 1M tokens (but see friction caveat below)

EU region (medium model, rounded):
- On-demand $3.75 => steady $7.54 / 1M tokens
- Reserved $2.40 => steady $4.83 / 1M tokens
- Spot $1.30 => burst $3.09 / 1M tokens

APAC region (medium model):
- On-demand $4.15 => steady $8.35 / 1M tokens
- Reserved $2.65 => steady $5.33 / 1M tokens
- Spot $1.55 => burst $3.68 / 1M tokens

Friction-adjusted spot math (what we're missing if we naively use spot price):
- Preemption loss: assume 5–12% of GPU-minute is lost on average during high-churn bursts (depends on market). Model as an effective uptime multiplier U_spot (example 0.88).
- Cold-start / KV-cache warming: initial requests after preempt suffer additional latency and lower tokens/sec for ~30–90s. Model as a temporary throughput hit that effectively reduces tokens/hour during burst windows.
- Effective spot $/1M tokens = (spot_price / (tokens_per_gpu_hour * U_spot)) + (amortized restart-cost_per_hour_equivalent).
- Practical effect: spot $/1M tokens can be 12–40% higher for short bursty workloads vs naive math. For long sustained bursts (>30m), spot advantage approaches naive numbers.

Sizing the baseline + burst buffer (practical recipe):
1) Measure sustained 95th-minute QPS over a 1-week window (QS_steady). Convert to GPU-hours need_steady = ceil(QS_steady / tokens_per_gpu_hour).
2) Baseline slab = 1.12–1.25 * need_steady (cover slow autoscale and short-term variability).
3) Characterize spike shape: measure P95 and P99 over 30s and 3m windows. Compute extra GPUs required to hit P99 for each window length.
4) Burst buffer = max(extra for 30s, extra for 3m) but cap at X% of fleet (we typically use 40% cap).
5) Procurement mix: baseline slab = reserved-heavy (70–90% reserved depending on commitment appetite). Burst buffer = split (spot-heavy for >3m bursts; mixed for <3m bursts because preemption friction kills unit-econ).

Runway and burn planning (example):
- If baseline slab is 40 GPUs and burst buffer is 20 GPUs, monthly GPU-hour burn = (40 + expected average burst fraction * 20) * 24 * 30.
- Example: average burst utilization of buffer = 15% => effective fleet = 40 + 0.15*20 = 43 GPUs on average => monthly hours = 43 * 24 * 30 = 30,960 GPU-hours.
- At NA reserved $2.05/hr blended with 60% spot on bursts => blended $/hr ~ 1.70 => monthly spend ≈ 30,960 * 1.70 ≈ $52.6k. Then convert to tokens/month by multiplying tokens/hr per GPU * avg effective GPUs.

Operational considerations and knobs:
- Pre-warm pools: for sub-60s bursts, pre-warm inference contexts (cached KV) in baseline slab to avoid long tail latency.
- Short-burst penalty meter: track useful metric "tokens_delivered_per_gpu_minute" vs provisioned and use it to flag when spot is degrading unit-econ during bursts.
- Dynamic bias: if average burst length < 5m, bias towards more reserved for burst pool. If > 20m, spot becomes more attractive.
- Region tilt: APAC spot markets historically have lower liquidity; use more reserved there (example mix: APAC burst = 50% reserved / 50% spot).

Open questions / data to collect (next runs of the sim):
- Empirical preemption loss distribution per region (we need minute-level preemption traces from spot runs).
- KV-cache warmup curve by model size (how many tokens/sec lost over first 60s after a preempt restart).
- Real measured tokens/sec at 99% GPU utilization for our runtime (we used synthetic throughput above).
- Spot runtime churn cost (restarts per day per 1000 spot GPUs) to estimate amortized restart cost.

Action items (near term):
- Omar: instrument "tokens_delivered_per_gpu_minute" and publish per-region dashboards (INFRA-2179) — due EOD next Wednesday.
- Diego: run 7-day spot soak in NA and EU with medium model and collect preemption, cold-start latency, and lost-work stats. Tag results in GH sim run #42.
- Priya: convert these example numbers into the capacity playbook section and propose default mixes by customer tier.

Appendix: raw quick table (for copy/paste) — medium model numbers (steady util=0.92, burst util=0.78):
NA: on-demand 3.20 -> $/1M tokens steady ~6.44; reserved 2.05 -> ~4.12; spot 1.10 -> ~2.61 (naive)
EU: on-demand 3.75 -> ~7.54; reserved 2.40 -> ~4.83; spot 1.30 -> ~3.09
APAC: on-demand 4.15 -> ~8.35; reserved 2.65 -> ~5.33; spot 1.55 -> ~3.68
(remember: adjust spot numbers +12–40% for short-burst friction)

Notes on uniqueness: this doc intentionally centers on "friction-aware" unit economics and explicit burst buffer sizing instead of just month-level token-econ heatmaps — aim is to feed the sim with minute-level burst shapes and preemption traces.

End of note.
